sections.title: ShadowFormer: Global Context Helps Image Shadow Removal
sections.content_md:
ShadowFormer: Global Context Helps Image Shadow Removal

Lanqing Guo 1

sections.title: Problem
sections.content_md: Existing deep learning methods for image shadow removal often suffer from severe artifacts around shadow boundaries and inconsistent illumination because they focus locally and ignore the global contextual correlation between shadow and non-shadow regions.

sections.title: Core Idea
sections.content_md: ShadowFormer is a lightweight, single-stage transformer-based network designed for end-to-end image shadow removal. It employs a multi-scale channel attention encoder-decoder architecture to efficiently capture hierarchical global information. At the bottleneck stage, a novel Shadow-Interaction Module (SIM) utilizes Shadow-Interaction Attention (SIA) to model the contextual correlation between shadow and non-shadow regions, leveraging the non-shadow areas to guide the restoration of shadow regions for improved illumination and color consistency.

sections.title: Method
sections.content_md:
ShadowFormer is a lightweight, single-stage transformer-based network designed for end-to-end image shadow removal. It employs a multi-scale channel attention encoder-decoder architecture to efficiently capture hierarchical global information. At the bottleneck stage, a novel Shadow-Interaction Module (SIM) utilizes Shadow-Interaction Attention (SIA) to model the contextual correlation between shadow and non-shadow regions, leveraging the non-shadow areas to guide the restoration of shadow regions for improved illumination and color consistency.

**Key Formulas:**
- $$ \mathbf{I}_{s} = \mathbf{I}_m \odot \mathbf{L}_{s} \odot \mathbf{R} + (1-\mathbf{I}_m) \odot \mathbf{L}_{ns} \odot \mathbf{R} $$
  The Retinex-based shadow model decomposing the shadow image into shadow and non-shadow regions based on illumination and reflectance.
- $$ \text{SIA}(\mathbf{X}, \mathbf{\Sigma}) = \text{softmax}(\frac{\mathbf{Q}\mathbf{K}^T}{d})\mathbf{V} $$
  The Shadow-Interaction Attention mechanism that reweights attention maps using correlation maps to emphasize context between shadow and non-shadow patches.
- $$ \mathcal{L}(\mathbf{I}_{gt},\; \hat{\mathbf{I}})=\left\|\mathbf{I}_{gt}-\hat{\mathbf{I}}\right\| $$
  The loss function used to train the network, measuring the difference between the ground truth and the predicted shadow-free image.

**Takeaways:**
- The proposed method effectively alleviates contour artifacts and improves illumination/color consistency by leveraging global context from non-shadow regions
- proving that a lightweight
- single-stage transformer can outperform complex

sections.title: Contributions
sections.content_md:
- **[theory]** We introduce a Retinex-based shadow model, which formulates the degradation of shadow and motivates us to exploit the global contexts for shadow removal.
- **[method]** We propose a new single-stage transformer for shadow removal (ShadowFormer) based on the multi-scale channel attention framework.
- **[method]** We propose a Shadow-Interaction Module with Shadow-Interaction Attention in the ShadowFormer to exploit the global contextual correlation between shadow and non-shadow regions.
- **[application]** The comprehensive experimental results on the public ISTD, ISTD+, and SRD datasets show that the proposed ShadowFormer achieved a new state-of-the-art performance with a very lightweight network, i.e., using up to 150x fewer model parameters.

sections.content_md:

The channel attention transformer-based encoder and decoder are to extract hierarchical information from the input shadow image, and to reconstruct the shadow-free image, respectively, using a series of channel attention (CA) modules. In the bottleneck stage, we adopt a Shadow-Interaction Module (SIM) to exploit the context information across both spatial and channel dimensions from non-shadow region to help shadow region restoration.

The detailed architectures of ShadowFormer model components. (a) Channel Attention (CA) Module in the encoder and decoder.
